description:
The Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme under the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (K.B.O.C.W.W.B) was launched in the state of Kerala. 

This scheme was initiated to provide financial assistance to the families of deceased construction workers. 

The scheme was officially launched on 1st January 2019. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to offer financial support to the families of construction workers who die while engaged in their work. 

The scheme aims to alleviate the financial burden on the families during the time of bereavement. 

Under this scheme, an ex-gratia amount of ₹20,000 is provided to the family of the deceased worker. 

This financial assistance is intended to cover funeral expenses and other immediate costs associated with the death. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for low-income families who may struggle to afford funeral costs. 

Eligibility for the scheme is specifically targeted at construction workers who are registered with the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

To qualify, the worker must have been actively engaged in construction work at the time of death. 

The worker must also have contributed to the welfare fund for a minimum of one year prior to their death. 

The age limit for eligibility is not strictly defined; however, the worker must be a legal adult at the time of registration. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

The application process for the Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme is straightforward. 

The family members of the deceased worker must submit an application to the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The application must include a death certificate of the worker. 

Additionally, the family must provide proof of the worker's registration with the welfare board. 

Documents such as identity proof and bank account details of the beneficiary are also required. 

The application can be submitted either online or in person at the local welfare board office. 

Once the application is received, it is processed by the welfare board. 

The disbursement of the ex-gratia amount is typically completed within 15 days of application approval. 

The scheme is implemented by the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

This board operates under the Department of Labour and Skills, Government of Kerala. 

The contact details for the board can be found on their official website. 

The board also provides additional welfare measures for construction workers, including health insurance and pension schemes. 

The Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme is part of a broader effort by the Kerala government to support the welfare of construction workers. 

As of October 2023, the scheme has benefited thousands of families across the state. 

The government has allocated significant funds to ensure the sustainability of this scheme. 

In the fiscal year 2022-2023, the Kerala government allocated ₹10 crore for the Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme. 

This allocation reflects the government's commitment to the welfare of construction workers and their families. 

The scheme has been well-received by the public and has garnered positive feedback from beneficiaries. 

Many families have expressed gratitude for the timely financial assistance during their time of need. 

The Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board continues to promote awareness about the scheme. 

This is done through various outreach programs and information sessions for construction workers. 

The board encourages all eligible workers to register and avail of the benefits of the scheme. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of social security measures aimed at protecting vulnerable workers in the construction sector. 

The construction industry in Kerala employs a significant number of workers, making this scheme crucial for their welfare. 

The government recognizes the risks associated with construction work and aims to provide a safety net for workers and their families. 

The Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme is a vital component of this safety net. 

In conclusion, the Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme under K.B.O.C.W.W.B is an essential welfare initiative. 

It provides crucial financial support to the families of deceased construction workers. 

The scheme is designed to ease the financial burden during a difficult time. 

With a clear application process and timely disbursement of funds, it serves as a lifeline for many families in Kerala. 

The commitment of the Kerala government to the welfare of construction workers is commendable. 

The ongoing support and funding for this scheme reflect a proactive approach to social welfare. 

Families of construction workers can rely on this scheme for assistance during their time of need. 

Overall, the Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme is a significant step towards ensuring the welfare and security of construction workers in Kerala. 

The scheme stands as a testament to the government's dedication to improving the lives of its citizens. 

For further information, interested parties are encouraged to visit the official website of the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

This website provides comprehensive details about the scheme and other welfare initiatives available for construction workers. 

The Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme is an important resource that should be utilized by eligible families. 

In a state where construction work is prevalent, such schemes play a crucial role in supporting workers and their families. 

The Kerala government continues to evaluate and improve welfare schemes to meet the needs of its citizens effectively. 

This ensures that the benefits reach those who need them the most. 

The Funeral and Ex-Gratia Scheme is a prime example of such efforts.
